pretreatments.description: Knife Milling (KM) - A mechanical pretreatment technology using a knife mill inside a milling chamber with mobile milling elements mounted on a central shaft for substrates with total solids content higher than 85%. Knife mills apply forces to disaggregate solid particles, slice the fibers, and produce small pieces (similar to chopping with a knife). BGP1 used this to improve anaerobic degradability of mixed vegetable seeds and avoid sedimentation in digesters.

Hammer Mill (HM) - A mechanical pretreatment technology using a rotor with a set of attached hammers that impact material against a breaker plate to grind fibers into long and thin pieces. HM grinds similar to a mortar and pestle. BGP2 used this to improve kinetic of biogas formation and avoid floating layers in digesters.

Extruder (EX) - A mechanical pretreatment technology where raw materials are fed into one end and transported along the barrel with a driving screw, subjected to friction heat, mixing, and vigorous shearing upon pressure release at the finishing end. Extrusion causes considerable abrasion of the material upon pressure release, breaking down cell walls and causing structural changes for easy digestion. BGP3 used this to improve anaerobic degradability.

Wet Shredder + Hydrodynamic Cavitation (SHC) - A combination system using a wet shredder with integrated heavy material separator and a hydrodynamic cavitation reactor with stator and rotor assembly for generation of cavitation. Used to avoid crust and floating layers in digesters without blocking pump and pipe systems.
